rationale: One major patch finding: the enum coercion `LiteLLMBudgetCategory(category.value)` in `_mirror_budget_assignment` is unguarded. Both enums are currently identical (platform/cli/premium_models — verified by edge-case lens reading both files), so no failure today. However, the function is now a generic helper callable with any future `CoreBudgetCategory` value; if `CoreBudgetCategory` gains a member before `LiteLLMBudgetCategory` is updated, `ValueError` propagates synchronously through `_configure_direct_runtime_overrides` and aborts LLM model creation for that request. Fix is a one-line try/except. All 8 acceptance criteria pass and all three review lenses ran cleanly. 2 deferred/dismissed findings (blind lens flagged platform-budget skip — intentional per spec three-way priority; commit format uses Conventional Commits style rather than documented ticket-prefix style — squash-merge resolves).

findings.problem: LiteLLMBudgetCategory(category.value) is unguarded. Both enums currently share identical values, but the conversion raises ValueError for any CoreBudgetCategory value not present in LiteLLMBudgetCategory. With the old hardcoded PLATFORM constant this was impossible; the generalization to accept any CoreBudgetCategory introduced the failure mode.
findings.impact: A future CoreBudgetCategory value without a matching LiteLLMBudgetCategory member causes ValueError to propagate synchronously through _configure_direct_runtime_overrides (no handler), aborting the entire LLM model creation call for that request.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the conversion in try/except ValueError and return early: `try: litellm_cat = LiteLLMBudgetCategory(category.value) except ValueError: logger.warning('Unknown budget category %r, skipping mirror', category.value); return`. Alternatively add a unit test asserting both enums have identical values, which fails at the point of divergence rather than silently breaking the hot path.
